newsitem.title: USA: Money managers still neutral on U.S. debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers still neutral on U.S. debt -- survey.

text.p: Money managers remained neutral-to-moderately bullish in U.S. debt markets last week amid the Treasury's $39.75 billion quarterly refunding, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"The data suggests that money managers were more involved in the refunding auctions than the survey suggested would be the case last week," the report said.
"Nonetheless, changes in portfolio structure are still modest, suggesting that auction participation was tempered," it said.
In the week ended February 18, duration bogey slipped to 4.14 from 4.15 on an arithmetic basis and dropped to 4.67 from 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 5.28 from 5.37 on an arithmetic basis. It held steady at 5.02 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.02 percent from 7.16 percent.
Twenty-four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, sharply up from eight percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active fell to 4.83 from 7.00 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
